source_text: We can restart once we have sorted out this business about critical parameters.  I'd say each variable in the Lean model needs an interpretation in terms of real countable things, and the requirement should be that all countable things need to be taken into account at some point in the model in a meaningful way, or we have a facade on our hands again.

reply_text:
Understood: the restart waits until the critical parameters are sorted. I've written your requirement into the incident as a closing condition, with a first count of the real things, and extended codex-6's audit to cover it (commit `b22588832`).

**The requirement as recorded, in two directions:**

- **Model to world.** Every variable, parameter and index set in the Lean names the real, countable thing it stands for and how to count it. A variable with no such reading is a finding. So is one supplied at 1 where the real thing has hundreds.
- **World to model.** Every countable thing the machine exists to deal with appears in the model in a way that can change what the machine does. A thing that is absent, or present only as a name, is a finding.

**First count of the real things:**

| Countable thing | Count today | In the machine today |
|---|---|---|
| Open missions | 221 | in the field |
| Open excursions | 373 | absent from the decision |
| Open tickets | 43 | in the field |
| Patterns in the library | 1,431 in 120 families | 2 available to the constructor |
| Agent seats | 56 registered (29 Codex, 12 Claude, 10 Kimi, 4 Zai, 1 wm) | 3 fixed seats |
| Completed runs | 76 records | not read by selection |
| Run outcomes | 1 grounded change, 3 author refusals, and the rest | not counted |
| Stack claims | 417 | covered by the model |
| Repair findings | 153 | not yet checked |
| Steps in a horizon | 4 | preference stated at 1 of 4 |

The three task counts come from yesterday's census. Two rows are left uncounted for now: acceptance items on open tasks, and closed tasks. My quick file count for those matched worktree copies as well, so the numbers were inflated. I'd sooner leave a gap than give you a wrong figure.

**What codex-6 now has to add to the audit:**

1. For every variable and carrier type in the Lean: the real thing it stands for, how to count it, its count today, and the count the live machine actually supplied.
2. For every row above: where it enters the Lean and whether it can change anything there, or "absent", or "name only".
3. The Lean form of the requirement. That is a coverage statement that fails when a carrier is instantiated degenerately, plus what each run record must carry so the counts can be recomputed at run time.
4. Which of these are the critical parameters an alert to you has to watch on every run.

The addendum is `invoke-1790755497210-28911-38420ca6`, parked under `park-e75b48f6…` with a 60-minute deadline. When it lands I'll fill in the model side of the table and bring you the list of variables with no real reading and the things the model leaves out. The alert and its tripwire get built from that list, and then the restart question comes back to you.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-1
previous_reply_acts.text: **On the whitelist.** What the records and `PROOF-2b.md` show is five hand-written target files from 17 September, not three. Four of those targets were later finished. Between 2 and 21 targets had candidates on 20–21 September, and there was one target in almost every record from 22 September onward. So the facade you first noticed and the one-policy facade are the same mechanism, which narrowed over time.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-1
previous_reply_acts.text: **Why there was no alert.** The machine has thirteen tripwires, T1 to T13, and none of them watches any of these numbers. The values were in every run record and in no report. My own reports to you talked about selections and refusals and never gave the size of what was being chosen among.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-1
previous_reply_acts.text:
- **My reports.** These eight numbers head every report I make about a run, before anything else is said about it.
- **The machine.** A run whose critical parameters are degenerate raises an alert addressed to you and is not reported as a selection. The report belongs to the records owner and the tripwire to the controller owner. I'll send those handoffs once codex-6's audit is back, because the audit should name the full list of parameters that need watching, and these eight are only the ones I've found so far.
